item.title: Tourism
item.description: Planning trips, sightseeing and the effects of tourism.

children.definition: the place that someone is travelling to
children.example: Samarkand is a popular destination for history lovers.

children.definition: a detailed plan of a journey, with places and times
children.example: Our itinerary includes two days in Bukhara and one in Khiva.

children.definition: a place to stay, such as a hotel or guesthouse
children.example: We booked accommodation near the old city.

children.definition: the activity of visiting interesting places as a tourist
children.example: We spent the afternoon sightseeing in Khiva.

children.definition: a famous building or place that is easy to recognise
children.example: The Registan is Samarkand's best-known landmark.

children.definition: far away from the places that most tourists visit
children.example: We found a quiet village off the beaten track in the mountains.

children.definition: something you buy to help you remember a place you visited
children.example: I bought a ceramic plate from Rishtan as a souvenir.

children.definition: a visit to a place with a guide who explains things to you
children.example: We took a guided tour of the old city.

children.definition: a holiday where the travel and the hotel are sold together at one price
children.example: A package holiday can be cheaper than booking everything separately.

children.definition: a tired, confused feeling after a long flight to a different time zone
children.example: I had terrible jet lag after flying to New York.

children.definition: with too many people in one place
children.example: The beach was overcrowded in August.

children.definition: friendly and generous behaviour towards guests
children.example: Many visitors remember Uzbek hospitality long after their trip.
